The fixed-cap indicator converges on the strip except on its null facet intersection, so total and cap derivatives are the stated facet integrals for both signs. The same argument at an interval endpoint uses signed length and counting measure.

Proper old cuts have continuous section area, and at a regular nonproper cut the limiting projected section is surface-null or empty. Its neighboring section areas tend to zero by compactness and shrinking neighborhoods. Fubini gives the threshold derivative −S_j, and the simultaneous change in the strip integral is o(|t|) off the same null set.

Taking δ_j=(c_j−q′)/S_j with q′ the response-weighted sum gives common first budget and zero weighted threshold sum with weights ρ. A minimal positive dependence has one-dimensional kernel, so at each base the margin image is the entire affine hyperplane of the fixed ρ-weighted sum. It covers the plane exactly when that sum is nonnegative, and the chosen shifts preserve this.

The same caps still cover every deepest base plane, and the hypothesis retains the strict cover on other bases. After dividing their common first budget by the mixed mass, local minimality along both signs forces q′−βm=0. The resulting affine neutrality and canonical cuts are precisely the hypotheses of the linked simplex facet lemma.
